text.title: Design System Impact Queue Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether an empowered triage slot exists, then on what an incoming item actually describes and how many independent call-sites it carries, to decide between skipping, routing out to a bug tracker, holding at local-override, and promoting to roadmap.

decision-tree.root-question: Is there a fixed recurring review slot with a named attendee who can assign pillar owners on the spot?

branch.when: no recurring slot, or the attendee present cannot assign owners

conclusion.verdict: skip; a queue nobody can triage only accumulates — secure the slot via design-system-governance first

branch.when: the system has a single consuming surface, where drift surfaces in ordinary code review

conclusion.verdict: skip; for per-sprint drift capture against a spec use design-qa-during-build instead

branch.when: a recurring empowered slot exists and two or more surfaces consume the system
branch.question: What does the incoming item actually describe?

branch.when: an existing component failing its own published spec — a defect, not an evolution

conclusion.verdict: route out at intake; file it in that component's issue tracker and record the issue id on the queue item

branch.when: a wish phrased as a request — 'we need a better card' — with no observed instance behind it

conclusion.verdict: reject at intake; return it for the screen or file path, Figma node id, the hardcoded value actually observed, and the token that should have existed

branch.when: a concrete call-site: an observed hardcoded value or one-off pattern with its location recorded
branch.question: How many independent call-sites does the item now carry, and across how many distinct surfaces?

branch.when: fewer than three call-sites, or all three from a single surface

conclusion.verdict: triage as local-override; append the call-site to the item so the count can accumulate, and do not promote to roadmap yet

branch.when: three or more independent call-sites from at least two different surfaces, but accepted/in-progress is already at the WIP cap

conclusion.verdict: hold in accepted-pending; promote at the next window once WIP frees, and auto-escalate or close with a recorded reason if it misses two consecutive windows

branch.when: three or more independent call-sites from at least two surfaces, and WIP headroom exists

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; promote to roadmap, assign the pillar owner through the governance ownership map with the reporter recorded separately, and close from the fixed reason enum
